clue.text: Raised voice in argy-bargy following short trip

explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts FALL to FAL; ARGY-BARGY is British slang for a noisy quarrel, and a SET-TO is a brief fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is an artificially high singing or speaking voice, above the normal register.

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the article sits below the other piece

explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest or healer who mediates with the spirit world.

clue.text: Old king's reasonable line in speech

parts.note: reasonable means fair and a line is a row

explanation.surface: A monarch of old possesses a sensible queue, spoken of aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, FAIR ROW matches the Egyptian ruler's title; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a ruler of ancient Egypt, so an old king.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means earlier or previous
in a monastery, the monk ranking just below the abbot holds this title

explanation.definitionFit: The word means earlier as an adjective and names the monk second to an abbot as a noun.

parts.note: threepence is literally one half of the old sixpenny coin, so a show about threepence is jokily that

explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a British stage musical starring Tommy Steele, punningly linked to threepence.

clue.text: After hour, girl returned hair dye

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, lemonade usually means a sparkling lemon-flavoured soft drink.
